# Setup

Two questions this notebook answers, both at the level of *people*, not timecourses
(see `plot_concordance_isc_timecourses.qmd` for the time-resolved comparisons):

1. **Does a person's ISC level predict their concordance level?** Each adult's own
   leave-one-out-style ISC (their average pairwise ISC across everyone else) vs. their
   leave-one-out-style concordance (same averaging, over the PAIRWISE concordance file --
   not the group-vs-individual metric -- so both axes are built identically), correlated
   across people, per block.
2. **Which metric's "who is most/least similar to whom" pattern is trait-like, i.e.
   reproducible across blocks?** Builds a participant x participant similarity matrix per
   block per pairwise metric, then correlates the *same dyads'* values between every pair
   of blocks. A metric where pair A-B stays relatively high (or low) across different
   blocks has more individual-differences signal than one that's just noise each time.

Both parts use the two PAIRWISE/dyadic metrics only (concordance pairwise, ISC pairwise),
never the group-vs-individual concordance metric -- that one has no dyad identity by
construction, so it can't answer either "individual differences between specific people"
question here. See `plot_concordance_isc_timecourses.qmd` for analyses that do use it.

Reads, not recomputes:

- `data/results/concordance/fixation_density_concordance_dyadic.csv` -- one row per
  (video, pid_a, pid_b), each pair's r averaged across that video's windows; written by
  `calc_concordance_pairwise.R` (added alongside its existing window-level output
  specifically to support this notebook -- see that script's header).
- `data/results/isc/isc_fixation_pairwise.csv` -- pre-existing per-dyad, per-clip ISC
  (adults-adults/adults-kids/kids-kids), not windowed.
- `data/local_cache/participant_summary.csv` -- used to restrict ISC's own (larger) adult
  population down to concordance's `valid_data==TRUE` adults, same reasoning as
  `isc_analysis.qmd`'s Part 8b export (see METHODS_DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-02).

NOTE: `data/` is a symlink to the mounted lab server in this repo. Saves figures to
`figures/concordance/` (same topic as the timecourse notebook).

"Concordance" here is never "ISC" -- see `calc_concordance_group.R`'s header for the
naming rule.

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggthemes)
library(glue)
library(here)

CONCORDANCE_DYADIC_PATH <- here("data", "results", "concordance", "fixation_density_concordance_dyadic.csv")
ISC_PAIRWISE_PATH       <- here("data", "results", "isc", "isc_fixation_pairwise.csv")
PARTICIPANT_SUMMARY_PATH <- here("data", "local_cache", "participant_summary.csv")
FIGURES_DIR             <- here("figures", "concordance")
dir.create(FIGURES_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

ISC_COLOR      <- "#eb6834"
PAIRWISE_COLOR <- "#1baf7a"

BLOCKS <- list(
  frank  = c("frank_complex", "frank_objects", "frank_play"),
  sesame = c("sesameus_1", "sesameus_2", "sesameindia_1", "sesameindia_2"),
  slow   = c("slow_animals", "slow_hands", "slow_inanimate", "slow_people"),
  pixar  = c("pixar_birds")
)
video_to_block <- enframe(BLOCKS, name = "block", value = "video_name") |> unnest(video_name)

concordance_dyadic_raw <- read_csv(CONCORDANCE_DYADIC_PATH, show_col_types = FALSE)
isc_pairwise_raw_all   <- read_csv(ISC_PAIRWISE_PATH, show_col_types = FALSE)
participant_summary    <- read_csv(PARTICIPANT_SUMMARY_PATH, show_col_types = FALSE)

valid_adult_pids <- participant_summary |>
  filter(participant_type == "adults", valid_data == TRUE) |>
  pull(participant_id)

# Population-match ISC's own (larger) adult list down to concordance's population.
isc_pairwise_raw <- isc_pairwise_raw_all |>
  filter(comparison == "adults-adults", pid_a %in% valid_adult_pids, pid_b %in% valid_adult_pids)

isc_theme <- theme_few(base_size = 13) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank())
```

---

# Part A: Does a Person's ISC Predict Their Concordance?

```{r person-level-build}
# Leave-one-out-style per-person value for a dyadic metric: average this person's pairwise
# value across every dyad they're in (pid appears as either pid_a or pid_b, so stack both).
# Used identically for both metrics below so the two axes are built the same way.
person_level_from_dyads <- function(dyadic_df, value_col, out_col) {
  bind_rows(
    dyadic_df |> transmute(pid = pid_a, video_name, value = .data[[value_col]]),
    dyadic_df |> transmute(pid = pid_b, video_name, value = .data[[value_col]])
  ) |>
    group_by(pid, video_name) |>
    summarise(value = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    left_join(video_to_block, by = "video_name") |>
    group_by(pid, block) |>
    summarise(!!out_col := mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
}

person_concordance <- person_level_from_dyads(concordance_dyadic_raw, "mean_r", "concordance")
person_isc         <- person_level_from_dyads(isc_pairwise_raw, "isc_xy", "isc")

person_level <- inner_join(person_concordance, person_isc, by = c("pid", "block")) |>
  mutate(block = factor(block, levels = names(BLOCKS)))

block_cors <- person_level |>
  group_by(block) |>
  summarise(r = cor(isc, concordance, use = "complete.obs"), n = n(), .groups = "drop")

overall_r <- cor(person_level$isc, person_level$concordance, use = "complete.obs")
```

```{r person-level-plot, fig.height=7}
pA <- ggplot(person_level, aes(x = isc, y = concordance)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, colour = PAIRWISE_COLOR, size = 2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_text(data = block_cors, aes(label = glue("r = {round(r, 2)}  (n={n})")),
            x = -Inf, y = Inf, hjust = -0.08, vjust = 1.5, inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 4) +
  facet_wrap(~block, scales = "free") +
  labs(title = "Person-level ISC vs. concordance, by block (both pairwise)",
       subtitle = glue("Overall pooled r = {round(overall_r, 2)} (n={nrow(person_level)} person-block observations)"),
       x = "Person's mean ISC (avg. across their dyads, adults-adults)",
       y = "Person's mean concordance (avg. across their dyads, pairwise)") +
  isc_theme

pA
ggsave(file.path(FIGURES_DIR, "person_isc_vs_concordance_by_block.png"), pA, width = 10, height = 8)
```

---

# Part B: Cross-Block Reliability of Dyadic Similarity

For each pairwise metric, collapse each dyad to one value per block (averaging across
that block's clips), then correlate the *same dyads'* values between every pair of
blocks. A metric with higher cross-block r has a more trait-like, reproducible
individual-differences signal -- i.e. knowing A and B were unusually similar in one
block tells you something about whether they'll be similar in another.

(The group concordance metric -- individual vs. leave-one-out-group -- has no dyad
identity by construction, so it's excluded from this part; only the two pairwise
metrics apply.)

```{r dyadic-reliability-build}
canonicalize_pairs <- function(df, value_col) {
  df |>
    mutate(pid_lo = pmin(pid_a, pid_b), pid_hi = pmax(pid_a, pid_b)) |>
    left_join(video_to_block, by = "video_name") |>
    group_by(block, pid_lo, pid_hi) |>
    summarise(value = mean(.data[[value_col]], na.rm = TRUE), n_clips = n(), .groups = "drop")
}

concordance_dyad_block <- canonicalize_pairs(concordance_dyadic_raw, "mean_r")
isc_dyad_block         <- canonicalize_pairs(isc_pairwise_raw, "isc_xy")

block_pair_reliability <- function(dyad_block_df, metric_name) {
  blocks <- names(BLOCKS)
  combn(blocks, 2, simplify = FALSE) |>
    map_dfr(function(pair) {
      b1 <- pair[1]; b2 <- pair[2]
      d1 <- dyad_block_df |> filter(block == b1) |> select(pid_lo, pid_hi, value1 = value)
      d2 <- dyad_block_df |> filter(block == b2) |> select(pid_lo, pid_hi, value2 = value)
      joined <- inner_join(d1, d2, by = c("pid_lo", "pid_hi"))
      tibble(metric = metric_name, block_a = b1, block_b = b2,
             r = cor(joined$value1, joined$value2, use = "complete.obs"),
             n_dyads = nrow(joined))
    })
}

reliability_all <- bind_rows(
  block_pair_reliability(concordance_dyad_block, "Concordance (pairwise)"),
  block_pair_reliability(isc_dyad_block, "ISC (pairwise)")
) |>
  mutate(pair_label = glue("{block_a} x {block_b}"))

reliability_summary <- reliability_all |>
  group_by(metric) |>
  summarise(mean_r = mean(r), min_r = min(r), max_r = max(r), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r dyadic-reliability-plot, fig.height=5.5}
colors_b <- c("ISC (pairwise)" = ISC_COLOR, "Concordance (pairwise)" = PAIRWISE_COLOR)

pB <- ggplot(reliability_all, aes(x = pair_label, y = r, fill = metric)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), width = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colors_b) +
  labs(title = "Cross-block reliability of dyadic similarity",
       subtitle = str_wrap("Pearson r between the SAME participant pairs' metric values in two different blocks -- higher means who's-similar-to-whom carries over, i.e. more trait-like individual differences", width = 95),
       x = NULL, y = "Cross-block r (same dyads)", fill = NULL) +
  isc_theme + theme(legend.position = "top", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1))

pB
ggsave(file.path(FIGURES_DIR, "dyadic_reliability_across_blocks.png"), pB, width = 10, height = 6)
```

```{r dyadic-reliability-summary}
reliability_summary
```
